about.title: It started with a pair of AR glasses.
about.subtitle: The story behind why I work across so many layers.
about.exploreDescription: From the first lines of code to what I build today.

timeline.title: I started programming at 13
timeline.body: Small projects, lots of trial and error. It was the first time I realised I could make things instead of just using them.

timeline.title: I started building AR glasses as a teenager
timeline.body: I wanted AR glasses I couldn’t buy, so I tried to build them. Prototype after prototype, I learned 3D printing, optics, electronics and Unity.

timeline.title: The prototype left my room
timeline.body: Glassear won the 2nd Professional Prize at Maker Faire Galicia 2018. Around then I started giving talks at technology events and schools, explaining what I was building and how.

timeline.title: Learning from teams that did it for a living
timeline.body: At the Computer Vision Center I built an Android app for pose, face and object detection. At ManoMotion, in Stockholm, I worked on hand tracking and AR interfaces in Unity.
timeline.imageCaption: Pictured with Edgar Riba, creator of Kornia (open-source computer vision library)

timeline.title: Barcelona, Montreal and GlassFood
timeline.body: I studied Computer Science at UAB and spent part of my final year at ÉTS Montréal. My final degree project, GlassFood, combined mixed reality and computer vision to recognise ingredients and show recipes.

timeline.title: Software people depend on
timeline.body: With Patient73 and FECAMM I helped bring accessible games to a rare-disease platform and organise game jams with universities and hospitals. As a freelancer I built the Hess Test web application for Evalua-lo.
timeline.imageCaption: Presenting the second Patient73 Game Jam at RCDE Stadium.

timeline.title: GlassMusic meets real people
timeline.body: I brought GlassMusic to 4YFN in 2025 and 2026 so people could try Glassear and discover the project. Along the way, ACCIÓ selected Glassear among the 50 Catalan startups with the most potential.
timeline.imageCaption: The GlassMusic presentation from MWC 2026 is available, download it here

timeline.title: Still building, with more at stake
timeline.body: I'm CTO at TopBrokers, running AI, automation and production infrastructure, and I keep building Glassear, now with Glassear Studio: AI agents that help create spatial apps. It's the same journey that started with a pair of glasses.

about.intro: I started programming at 13. In 2015, still a teenager, I wanted AR glasses I couldn't buy, so I tried to build them. Glassear needed hardware, so I learned hardware. It needed computer vision, so I learned computer vision. Later came backend, infrastructure and AI. The technologies kept changing; the habit didn't: pick a hard problem, build it, break it, understand why, and build it again.
about.museumIntro: Photos, prototypes and moments along the way: from my first lines of code to the products I build today.
about.museumContinuation: The exhibition is still growing: I’m building the next chapter.

items.title: CTO
items.description: As CTO at TopBrokers.io, I work on software architecture and development, APIs and automation. I also manage infrastructure, deployment and production operations.
items.moreInfo:
Architecture & Systems: Designed backend microservices and RESTful APIs managing high-reliability transaction workflows and real-time data ingestion.

Infrastructure & Ops: Managed bare-metal and cloud Linux servers, Docker containerization, Proxmox virtualization, networking, reverse proxies, automated backup strategies, and centralized monitoring/alerting.

Database & Storage: PostgreSQL schema design, indexing, replication, and query performance tuning.

Automation & Fleet: Built distributed automation systems and device/fleet management tooling for operational reliability.
items.summary: Hands-on CTO leading software architecture, backend engineering, and production operations for high-reliability systems.
highlights: Architect resilient distributed microservices, APIs, and real-time automation pipelines
Operate production Linux servers, Docker containerization, PostgreSQL, networking, and automated backups
Technical leadership and development, from architecture decisions to deployment

items.title: Founder & CEO
items.description: I started Glassear in 2015 to build AR glasses I couldn't buy, and I've kept iterating ever since. Today it's Glassear One, an optical see-through headset powered by the user's smartphone, plus Glassear Studio, an AI-native platform for creating spatial apps, and GlassMusic, its first real use case.
items.moreInfo:
Hardware & XR: Designed custom AR/MR optical systems, 3D printed mechanical enclosures, embedded electronics, and sensor integration. Developed computer vision pipelines (OpenCV, YOLO) and custom Android Java protocols (USB Accessory, Screen Recording API) for low-latency tethering. Unity 3D / AR Foundation runtime architecture.

Glassear Studio: Engineered a natural-language application creation platform featuring an AI Planner, Intent Graph, GLX schema, tool-based agents with MCP, and deterministic validation layers synchronized with the Unity runtime. Web platform built with React, TypeScript, Node.js.

Recognition: Selected among ACCIÓ's Top 50 Catalan startups (Catalan Pitch Competition 2025), GlassMusic at 4YFN/MWC 2025 and 2026, 2nd Professional Prize at Maker Faire Galicia 2018, Jury member in 2019, technical speaker at Google Developer Groups (GDG).
items.summary: Optical see-through AR hardware, an AI-native XR platform and a first real use case: GlassMusic.
highlights: Built Glassear Studio to create and modify XR applications through natural language
Architected custom AR headset optics, embedded electronics, and real-time computer vision (OpenCV, YOLO)
Engineered low-latency Android Java USB accessory & screen recording protocols for Unity AR Foundation

items.title: Technical Lead
items.description: Collaboration with the non-profit organization Fecamm (Federació Catalana de malalties minoritàries), in the process of introducing games to their platform so that people with rare diseases can play. In relation to this, we have organized a month-long GameJam in collaboration with UAB, UPC, and various hospitals
items.summary: Led technical architecture and accessibility integration for a therapeutic gaming platform tailored for patients with rare diseases.
highlights: Engineered platform integration protocols and accessibility wrappers for motor-impaired input devices
Co-organized a month-long university & clinical GameJam in partnership with UAB, UPC, and hospitals

items.title: Freelance Developer
items.description: Development of the Hess Test: Creation of an application for psychological evaluation in human resources, with React on the frontend and PHP on the backend. The tool, scientifically validated by its creator, Gaspar, is used by companies in the sector for talent selection and analysis.
items.moreInfo: Implementation of databases, automated email sending, and user management in a WordPress-based environment. Use of processing queues for high performance in systems with limited resources, optimizing execution on shared hosting. Ensuring cross-platform compatibility and optimization for different devices and browsers. Development of the backend as a WordPress plugin, facilitating integration with other systems.
items.summary: Architected and delivered the production Hess Test: a scientifically validated psychological evaluation system for enterprise HR selection.
highlights: Built responsive React frontend with anti-tampering response validation and scoring state machines
Implemented high-performance backend queue processing and transactional email engines for resource-constrained hosting

items.title: Computer Vision internship
items.description: Development of AI applied to pose tracking, face tracking, and object tracking in an Android app created with Java.
items.moreInfo: My tutor was Edgar Riba, creator of Kornia, a library with over 10.4k stars on Github. Quote, 'Sometimes we forgot how young he was when assigning him tasks'.
items.summary: Developed real-time computer vision models for 6-DoF pose estimation, face tracking, and object tracking on mobile devices.
highlights: Mentored directly by Edgar Riba (creator of Kornia, 10k+ GitHub stars)
Optimized mobile neural network inference and low-level camera pipeline processing in Java & OpenCV

items.title: Hand Tracking AR/VR Internship
items.description: Development of AR applications for Glassear, using the ManoMotion SDK. Design of AR interfaces and optimization of hand tracking algorithms.
items.moreInfo: Work with OpenCV and neural networks to improve gesture detection. Certificate available at: https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:6559408874229760001/
items.summary: Integrated ManoMotion's 3D hand tracking SDK into Glassear AR hardware and Unity runtimes for gesture-based spatial computing.
highlights: Designed spatial interaction paradigms and gesture recognition pipelines for hands-free augmented reality
Implemented OpenCV and neural network processing filters to reduce tracking jitter under challenging lighting

items.title: Glassear & Glassear Studio
items.description: Mixed-reality glasses combining custom hardware and XR software. The project includes Glassear Studio, a tool for creating and modifying interactive applications through natural language.
items.story: I started building AR glasses as a teenager in 2015. More than a decade later, Glassear is real hardware, and Glassear Studio lets AI agents help create the apps that run on it.

items.name: Glassear

points: Glassear Studio — spatial creation with AI

points: MapAnim — an animated-map editor with video export

principles.title: A few things building taught me.

items.title: AI should do things, not just talk about them.
items.body: It gets interesting when a model can use real tools, change a real scene or call a real API, with deterministic checks around it deciding what actually happens.

items.title: The prototype is where the real work starts.
items.body: Making something work once is a demo. Making it work on an ordinary Tuesday, for someone else, with bad Wi-Fi, is a product.

items.title: I like owning the whole problem.
items.body: Frontend, backend, hardware, AI or infrastructure are implementation choices. If it's part of the product, it's part of the problem.

items.title: Emerging tech gets interesting when it stops feeling emerging.
items.body: AR and AI don't matter because they're new. They matter the day a musician reads a score hands-free, or a team stops doing something by hand.
